tweet.text:
Jensen closed his GTC Berlin 2026 keynote with this Hermes Agent demo as the finale. 

He introduced it by saying the way to build an agent is to ask an agent to build it for you, so he installed and set up a customized Hermes in one prompt. 

Then he used Hermes, running on @nvidia RTX Spark, to create a simulated training environment for the @huggingface Microduck. Hermes planned an obstacle course with Nemotron and had GPT-6 Astra build it using FreeCAD, Omniverse libraries, Blender, Newton, and Isaac Lab. Hermes trained thousands of simulated ducks on that course until the validated policy was ready to run on the real robot in the physical world.

At Nous, we believe open source is a practical tool as much as a philosophical ideal. It gives users the ability to build powerful, complex workflows chaining numerous local+cloud models, devices, and tools themselves instead of waiting for a company to enable them.

Papertrade: the collapse started before the transferability ban
Staker income on
@papertrade_xyz
fell from $6.7M a day (15 Oct) to $88K (21 Oct). CT blames the 19 Oct "PAPER stays non-transferable" post. The data doesn't support that.
TL;DR:
• $52.8M of the $57.8M paid to stakers was LP overflow, i.e. net trader losses passed through, not fees
• Staker take per volume fell from 0.52bp to 0.14bp on 17 Oct, two days before the announcement
• The ban removed the exit, not the demand: Paragon settled para:PAPER at $0.0263 and OI roughly halved in a day
• On 22 Oct 13:00 UTC the house LP hit its $5M cap again and overflow resumed: $691K to stakers in 24h
• The top 10 stakers lost $8.58M trading but have already earned $9.06M back, and still hold 1.34B PAPER
Full breakdown with valuation scenarios and charts:
https://x.com/zerokn0wledge_/status/2113306300591526027
Cheers, ZK!

tweet.text:
$6.7M a day to $88K a day in under a week.

That's what @papertrade_xyz paid its $PAPER stakers on the 15th vs the 21st of October.

CT has a clear culprit: the "PAPER stays non-transferable" post from the 19th. But the data actually shows that the collapse already started two days before that post. And the $62M of "revenue" that made Papertrade a top fee earner in crypto was never really revenue to begin with.

Wait what?

Let's talk about where the $62M came from.

Papertrade charges a 2% fee on realized PnL and liquidated margin, split 50/50 between stakers and the devs. Dev fees sit at $4.9M lifetime, so the entire fee pool was ~$9.8M.

The other ~$53M was LP overflow. The house LP is capped at $5M, and every dollar of net trader losses above that cap gets swept straight to stakers.

Uniswap now routes trades through external DEXs
Uniswap has launched Aggregator Hooks, connecting seven external liquidity sources, including Curve, Fluid and PancakeSwap, and making them accessible as Uniswap v4 pools.
The router automatically finds the best route across Uniswap pools and external venues, executing the trade in a single transaction.
The feature is available via Uniswap’s web app and API on Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain.
Swaps routed through external sources incur protocol fees, which are used to burn $UNI.
